summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and long-term warfarin use for recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for a two-day productive cough. Evaluation revealed pneumonia on chest X-ray and leukocytosis, prompting treatment with intravenous antibiotics. She also presented with a supratherapeutic INR of 9.4 without bleeding, managed with oral vitamin K and temporary discontinuation of warfarin. Her hemoglobin declined slightly but remained within her baseline range, and no transfusion was required. She improved clinically with resolution of fever and respiratory symptoms, stable oxygenation, and decreasing white count. She was discharged home after one night with a plan to complete oral antibiotics, close INR follow-up, and continuation of home medications including torsemide. No acute heart failure exacerbation or DVT was found.
problems: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Adverse effect of anticoagulants, initial encounter
